policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: The ASV body reads the direct imperative 'cease then,' distinguishing the qere וַחֲדָל from the ketiv third-person reading identified by the mapped textual-variant note as 'let him cease.'

The ASV body continues with the direct imperative 'And let me alone,' distinguishing the qere וְשִׁית; the mapped textual-variant note presents the alternative construction beginning 'let him cease,' whereas the ASV text directly addresses the one being told to leave Job alone.
